drug_class: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) — eye drop form
purpose: Nepafenac eye drops are used to treat pain and swelling in the eye after cataract surgery. They help reduce inflammation and discomfort during the healing process. In some cases, they are also used to lower the risk of a condition called macular edema, which is swelling in the back of the eye that can affect vision.
how_it_works: When your eye is irritated or has surgery, your body releases certain chemicals that cause pain and swelling. Nepafenac works by blocking those chemicals — specifically substances called prostaglandins — so your eye feels less inflamed and uncomfortable. Think of it like turning down the volume on your eye's pain and swelling response.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are temporary stinging or burning when you put the drops in, blurry vision right after use, feeling like something is in your eye, redness, and increased sensitivity to light. These effects are usually mild and short-lived.
warnings: Do not wear contact lenses while using this medication. Let your doctor know if you take blood thinners, since NSAIDs can sometimes affect bleeding. Use it exactly as prescribed — stopping early or using it longer than directed can cause problems. Rarely, NSAIDs eye drops can slow healing or affect the cornea, so report any new eye pain or vision changes right away.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop into the affected eye three times a day (for Nevanac) or once a day (for Ilevro), starting one day before cataract surgery and continuing through the first two weeks after surgery. Always follow your eye doctor's specific instructions, as your schedule may vary.
